page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-1 is an ARM-based general-purpose server powered by a single dedicated Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 physical core running at 3.0 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It features no local NVMe storage and does not include any GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals average single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core testing placing the instance in the middle 50% tier. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are limited, falling into the bottom 10% tier. Memory read-only bandwidth is recorded at 70.86 GB/sec for small cached blocks and drops to 11.99 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks. Single-threaded gzip compression achieves 23.65 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25% tier.

This server is a cost-efficient option for entry-level ARM development, software compilation testing, and lightweight general-purpose workloads. Due to its limited single-core resource profile and lower memory bandwidth, it is not recommended for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded applications, or high-throughput web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-1 is an entry-level, general-purpose server featuring a single dedicated Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 physical core clocked at 3.0 GHz and 4 GB of RAM. Operating on the arm64 architecture, this instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmarks indicate average single-core CPU performance, but multi-core, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall into the bottom 10% tier. It is best suited for lightweight ARM development, testing, and basic web serving.
